dno_dashboard.subtitle: ICE single-DSO monopoly · CNFL (ICE subsidiary) + 2 municipals + 4 cooperatives · 7 provincias · 84 cantones (LAU)
dno_dashboard.intro: Costa Rica's distribution sector is uniquely concentrated and constitutionally barred from for-profit private ownership (Ley 7593 + foundational ICE Decree-Law 449 / 1949). ICE direct (Instituto Costarricense de Electricidad, ~38% of customers, national rural + Caribbean + extra-metropolitan) and its wholly-owned subsidiary CNFL (Compañía Nacional de Fuerza y Luz, ~41%, Greater San José metropolitan area / GAM Central) together cover ~79% of distribution — the highest state-owned concentration in OECD. ESPH (Empresa de Servicios Públicos de Heredia, municipal, ~6%) and JASEC (Junta Administrativa del Servicio Eléctrico de Cartago, municipal, ~6%) cover the Heredia + Cartago provincias. Four rural electrification cooperatives (Coopelesca / Coopeguanacaste / Coopealfaro Ruiz / Coopesantos) hold the remaining ~9% in the rural northern + Pacific + Los Santos zones. This is the only OECD country where electricity distribution is constitutionally barred from for-profit private ownership.
